task.title: Page orientation, bleed and marks
task.shortdesc: A page can be turned a quarter turn after it is laid out. The PDF then tells viewers and printers to show it turned. Use this to put a wide table on a landscape page in a document of portrait pages, so that all the pages face the same way in the book. The page orientation, bleed and marks reference lists the descriptor used here.

context.p: The element names in the examples, such as wide, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML. explains @page rules and named pages.

step.cmd: Give the page a name and a size

info.p: Write a named page rule with the size that the content needs, and send the element to it with page:
The element starts on a new page, which is laid out in landscape. The pages after it are portrait again.
Add page-orientation to the named page rule:

CSSMedia lays out the page as usual and then turns it when it is shown: rotate-left turns it a quarter turn to the left (counterclockwise) and rotate-right a quarter turn to the right (clockwise). upright, the initial value, does not turn it. The landscape page of the example is then shown as a portrait page, with the table reading from the bottom to the top, as in a printed book.

The layout does not change: the margin boxes, the page number and the rest of the page are laid out on the page as it is, and they turn with it. A page that you do not name keeps upright, so only the pages of the named rule turn. You can also turn the pages of a selector, such as @page :left.

result.p: The pages that hold wide content are laid out in the size they need and shown turned, in line with the other pages.
